subject: zoology
question_text: Write a note on DFC. Give the significance in a terrestrial ecosystem.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.47, SAQ 58). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. SAME-UNIT OVERLAP: the detritus food chain is also one third of LAQ 10 (types of food chains, book p.26). This card is not a cut of that answer — it adds the significance in a terrestrial ecosystem, which the long answer does not ask for.

steps.label: What DFC is
lines: DFC stands for Detritus Food Chain.
It is a food chain that begins with dead
organic matter instead of with a living
green plant.
It is the important food chain of a
terrestrial ecosystem.
steps.why: The letters must be expanded first, and the one line that matters is where the chain STARTS — that starting point is the whole difference between a detritus chain and a grazing chain.
common_mistakes: Writing that a DFC starts with green plants. That is the GRAZING food chain.
Giving only the letters. The expansion carries the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Grazing chains start with something alive; detritus chains start with something dead.
steps.margin_note: Expand the letters, then say where the chain starts. Three lines.

steps.label: Detritus
lines: Detritus is the dead organic matter of an
ecosystem.
It is formed from leaf litter, dead bodies
and the faeces of animals.
steps.why: Detritus is a named material, so the answer lists what it is made of; a student who writes only dead matter has not shown what falls to the forest floor.
common_mistakes: Writing that detritus is soil. It is the dead ORGANIC matter lying on and in the soil.
Leaving out the faeces, which are one of the three named sources.
steps.memory_tip: Three sources of detritus: fallen leaves, dead bodies and droppings.
steps.margin_note: One definition line and one list line. Keep it to two lines.

steps.label: Decomposers
lines: Detritus carries decomposers, which are
heterotrophic organisms. Ex: fungi and
bacteria.
They meet their energy and nutrition needs
by degrading the detritus, so they are
called saprotrophs.
They secrete enzymes that break the detritus
down into simple absorbable substances.
steps.why: The decomposers are what turn detritus into a food chain, and the word saprotroph is the named term the answer must carry along with the two examples.
common_mistakes: Calling the decomposers producers. They are heterotrophs and cannot make their own food.
Leaving out the word saprotroph, which is the named term for this feeding mode.
steps.memory_tip: Saprotroph: enzymes go out on to the dead matter, the digested food comes back in.
steps.margin_note: Name the decomposers, the examples and the word saprotroph. Three short statements.

steps.label: Significance and examples

lines.text: The DFC returns dead matter to the soil

lines: The DFC breaks down the dead matter of a
terrestrial ecosystem and returns its
nutrients to the soil for the plants.
Without it, dead leaves and bodies would
pile up and the nutrients would be locked
away.
Ex-1: Detritus → Earthworms → Frogs →
Snakes.
Ex-2: Dead animals → Flies and maggots →
Frogs → Snakes.
steps.why: The question asks for the significance separately, so the recycling of nutrients is stated in its own step; the two chains are written last because they are the proof that detritus really does feed a chain of animals.
common_mistakes: Giving the chains and calling that the significance. The significance is the RETURN of nutrients to the soil.
Drawing the arrows backwards. An arrow points FROM the eaten TO the eater.
steps.memory_tip: Detritus feeders are the second trophic level: earthworms, flies and maggots come straight after the dead matter.
steps.margin_note: One statement of significance, then the two example chains with the arrows pointing forward.

insider_note: The question has two halves — the note and the significance — and the significance is the recycling of nutrients, not the example chains.
